Combined Immunotherapy and Hybrid Dose-Fraction Radiotherapy for Driver-Negative Metastatic NSCLC: A Phase II Trial with Parallel Preclinical Studies
Abstract
Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based chemoimmunotherapy has become a standard first-line treatment for patients with driver-negative metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the clinical benefit is limited. Radiotherapy has potential antitumor immunomodulatory effects, but the optimal dose and fractionation remain unclear. Methods: This single-arm, multicenter, prospective, phase II trial enrolled patients with stage IV driver-negative NSCLC who received first-line chemoimmunotherapy. During the ICI maintenance phase, patients received hybrid dose-fraction radiotherapy (Hybrid-RT): stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy (SABR) to targetable lesions and low-dose radiotherapy (LDRT) to other sites. Patients restaged to stage III disease after chemoimmunotherapy received short-course hypofractionated radiotherapy to all residual lesions. The primary endpoint was 1-year progression-free survival (PFS) rate. The secondary endpoints included 1-year overall survival (OS) rate, objective response rate, and safety. Parallel preclinical mechanistic studies were performed in a murine model. Results: A total of 83 patients were enrolled from 2022 May 9 to 2023 December 31. The 1-year PFS rate was 54.2% (median PFS 16.1 months; 95% confidence interval [CI] 11.4 to 19.2 months), meeting the primary endpoint.
